data.name: Red Spider: Vengeance
data.detailed_description:

Note: This software also includes the Remastered version released in 2024.

For more details about the Remastered version, please search for "Red Spider: Vengeance Remastered Free Ver." on Steam or refer to App ID: 3582550.

We're an indie game developer studio from Japan.
We're big fans of Hong Kong films and want to present the fascination of them.
Red Spider: Vengeance is a Hong Kong noir style visual novel inspired by many hong kong movies, especially Infernal Affairs series and Johnnie To's films.
There are 6 story routes with the different characters(approximately 105,000 words in total).

Synopysis

Yvet grew up as an orphan on the Mainland. She was taken in by a crime syndicate when she was young and trained as an assassin.

She killed many people, but she had her reasons for breaking out of that group. She escaped and married Francis, the leader of the Red Flower Society, an underworld mob that operated in Kowloon, Hong Kong.

One day, Francis was shot in a nightclub, and a doctor said that it was highly unlikely he would regain consciousness.

Yvet takes over his responsibilities and tries to find the person who was behind the shooting, with her bodyguards and a private detective she knew.

Playtime

Multiple Choices / 6 Routes Total / Approximately 7-8 hours (Just over 1 hour per route)

Features

The narrative of this game is a dedicated homage to numerous classic Hong Kong Noir films. Each character was written with a specific Hong Kong movie star in mind, imagining them to be the actor who would actually portray the role.

Details on which scenes reference which films, and which actors served as inspiration for each character, are all fully explained within the "Cyclopedia" included in the game.

reviews.review:
A VN set in Hong Kong criminal underworld about attempted assassination of a mob boss and his wife's attempt to rein the organization and investigate the attack. It's mostly straightforward, with story branches rather than actual choices, but it's decent enough crime story with some length. If you're familiar with John Woo's or Chow Yun Fat's crime movies, you'll feel right at home. And it's free!

Edit: Music by Yasunori Shiono, Lufia's composer. WTH.
